_comment: Every third-party artifact the Windows build downloads, pinned by URL +
sha256. build-windows.ps1 refuses a mismatching hash. To bump a dep:
update url/version, blank the sha256, run build-windows.ps1 -AcceptNewHashes
(it downloads, records the hash, and rewrites this file), then VERIFY the
new hash against the upstream project's published checksum before
committing. Rationale for each source lives in PACKAGING.md's dependency
kicad: BUNDLED, pruned. Stage-Kicad extracts this official installer's
payload minus $KicadPrune (3D models, demos, translations, python plugin
extras) into tools\kicad, so one eSim exe carries everything. Unlike the
old off-repo hand-maintained repack (which rotted), this is reproducible:
bump this entry, rebuild, and the smoke test re-proves the pruned tree

python.notes: Full private CPython (nuget layout: tools/ = the runtime). Unlike the 'embeddable' zip, pip works normally, which is how the PyQt6 wheel set is installed.

ngspice.notes: Official 64-bit Windows build with XSPICE code models. Same version the Ubuntu nghdl toolchain builds from source.

iverilog.notes: Bleyer's Windows Icarus build. FALLBACK ONLY (-SkipSimBuild): it ships without libvvp, so d_cosim cannot run with it - only the Verilog Verifier. The Full build compiles iverilog_source instead. It is an Inno Setup 6.1 installer, which 7-Zip cannot open: installed silently into a build dir, copied to library/bin/iverilog/, then uninstalled again. HASH PROVENANCE: bleyer.org publishes no checksum alongside the download, so unlike every other entry here this sha256 could NOT be cross-checked against an upstream-published value - it was recorded from the download (19165730 bytes, Last-Modified 2022-06-12) and is trust-on-first-use. The artifact is immutable (a dated v12 build), so a future mismatch means the upstream file changed and must be re-verified from a second network before -AcceptNewHashes is used on it.

iverilog_source.notes: Icarus Verilog source at the SAME pinned commit nghdl/install-nghdl.sh builds on Ubuntu (ICARUS_REF). Built inside the staged MSYS2 (mingw64) with --enable-libvvp - the one piece d_cosim needs that no prebuilt Windows Icarus provides - and staged under library/bin/iverilog/.

msys2.notes: Base MSYS2, then pacman installs mingw-w64-x86_64-{gcc,make,verilator,ghdl-llvm} plus the msys build tools (autotools/bison/flex/gperf/patch/make) inside it (see build-windows.ps1). Powers the OPTIONAL 'HDL toolchain' installer component (NgVeri code-model builds + NGHDL/GHDL VHDL co-sim) AND hosts the Stage-SimToolchain source builds. ghdl-llvm, NEVER ghdl-mcode: mcode cannot link the nghdl socket server (GHDL-BACKEND-26.04.md applies on Windows too).

kicad_installer.notes: Source payload for Stage-Kicad: extracted (7z -tNsis), pruned per $KicadPrune, staged at tools/kicad inside the ONE eSim installer. The installer exe itself never ships or runs. Fetched from KiCad's GitHub release (the identical file, same sha256): downloads.kicad.org ended this 1.1 GB download early on every attempt (2026-09-30).

innosetup.notes: Build-machine tool only (provides ISCC.exe); nothing from it ships inside the eSim installer. Hosted on GitHub releases -- jrsoftware pruned files.jrsoftware.org/is/6/ (older point releases 404 there).

mingw_gcc.notes: Build-machine tool only: compiles the eSim.exe launcher (gcc + windres) when MSYS2 is skipped (-SkipMsys); with MSYS2 staged its own mingw64 gcc is used instead. Nothing from it ships. sha256 matches the digest GitHub publishes for the release asset.
